handbookNote: Missouri State Highway Patrol (MSHP) Water Patrol Division boating safety program (mshp.dps.mo.gov) and the Missouri Revised Statutes Chapter 306 (boating law) and Chapter 577 (BUI/negligent operation) -- Missouri has no single official state-administered boating knowledge exam; RSMo 306.127 requires operators born after January 1, 1984 to hold a Missouri Boating Safety Identification Card (required since January 1, 2005, extending to those born on or after January 1, 2006 starting January 1, 2027), obtained by completing a NASBLA-approved boating safety course, passing a water patrol division equivalency exam, or holding a qualifying U.S. Coast Guard license -- in practice this means the NASBLA-approved course vendor's own embedded quiz IS the de facto test, not a separate state exam, confirmed independently by two sources: Boat-Ed's official Missouri course (boat-ed.com/missouri, live 2026) requiring at least 70% on unit quizzes and 80% on the final exam with unlimited retakes, and the BoatUS Foundation's Missouri page (boatus.org/missouri), which explicitly states its own free course is NOT approved by the Missouri State Water Patrol to satisfy the mandatory education requirement (recommending it only as a study aid for an approved course) -- this cross-confirms the mandate is real and enforced against a specific approved-vendor list rather than satisfied by any free course; the exact final-exam question count is not consistently published by Missouri's approved vendors and is therefore left unconfirmed rather than asserted -- content also grounded in real Missouri statute detail: vessel classification and equipment scaling by length (RSMo 306.100), PFD requirements for children under 7 (RSMo 306.220) and PWC riders (RSMo 306.142), minimum operating ages of 14 for motorboats (RSMo 306.122) and PWCs (RSMo 306.142), general operating/speed rules including a 30 mph nighttime cap and 100-foot no-wake zones near docks (RSMo 306.125), vessel registration through the Department of Revenue (RSMo 306.030), accident-reporting duties and the $500/injury reporting threshold (RSMo 306.140), the Water Patrol Division's statutory enforcement authority (RSMo 306.010), a 0.08% BUI blood alcohol threshold with escalating penalties (RSMo 577.014), negligent vessel operation (RSMo 577.025), and unlawful use of water skis/surfboards (RSMo 577.024) -- plus universal NASBLA-aligned boating-safety fundamentals (Navigation Rules, aids to navigation, PFD types, required equipment, cold-water immersion, weather, and towed water sports) applied to Missouri's major recreational reservoirs, including the Lake of the Ozarks and Table Rock Lake, which drive significant seasonal Water Patrol enforcement activity -- price matches this project's Motorcycle-tier boating convention ($7.99), not a placeholder
